# exposomeSC

*Study-aware, cell-type-resolved exposure association for population
single-cell transcriptomes*

[![DOI](https://img.shields.io/badge/DOI-10.18129%2FB9.bioc.exposomeSC-blue.svg)](https://doi.org/10.18129/B9.bioc.exposomeSC)
[![License:
Artistic-2.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-Artistic--2.0-blue.svg)](https://opensource.org/licenses/Artistic-2.0)

## What it does

`exposomeSC` tests donor-level exposures against gene expression within
a cell type, for single-cell RNA-seq cohorts in which each donor
contributes many cells. The exposure is a property of the donor, so
cells from one donor are measurements of the same unit rather than
independent replicates. The package therefore aggregates raw counts by
donor and cell type and fits a robust edgeR quasi-likelihood model per
cell type, with the donor as the unit of inference.

The case study the package was built around is smoking in the integrated
Human Lung Cell Atlas, and a small part of those data is shipped with
it. This README quotes no result; the tables and figures of the
vignettes are computed from the shipped data when they are built.

## Installation

``` r

# After Bioconductor acceptance:
if (!require("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE))
    install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::install("exposomeSC")

# Development version from GitHub:
BiocManager::install("CuiweiG/exposomeSC")
```

## A first analysis

The package ships a small real data set: 352 tracheal epithelial cells
from 12 donors of the Human Lung Cell Atlas, six heavy smokers and six
never smokers, with up to 10 basal, secretory and multiciliated-lineage
cells per donor.
[`?hlca_airway_subset`](reference/hlca_airway_subset.md) gives its
source, licence and selection rule. The data set shows how the functions
are called on real counts; with 12 donors and at most 10 cells per donor
and cell type it is far too small to support conclusions about smoking.
A second real data set,
[`?incov_pbmc_subset`](reference/incov_pbmc_subset.md), holds blood
cells of 43 patients with their surface proteins, plasma metabolites and
plasma levels of exogenous compounds, for the functions that need those.

``` r

library(exposomeSC)

scee <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "hlca_airway_subset.rds",
    package = "exposomeSC"))
scee

fit <- run_sc_exwas(scee,
    exposure = "smoking",
    covariates = "chemistry_v3")

head(fit[order(fit$pvalue),
         c("gene", "celltype", "log2FC", "statistic", "pvalue", "padj_global")])
```

The object was made by [`build_scee()`](reference/build_scee.md), which
checks that every donor in the cells has a row in the exposure matrix
and that every row belongs to a donor with cells; the script that made
the file checks that its counts are non-negative whole numbers.
[`run_sc_exwas()`](reference/run_sc_exwas.md) returns one row per gene
and cell type, with `padj_global` adjusted across the whole
gene-by-cell-type family.

For the default edgeR backend, `se` is `NA` by design: the
quasi-likelihood F test supplies no coefficient standard error, and
`statistic` is the signed square root of that F statistic, a ranking
quantity rather than a Wald statistic.

## What the estimate is

The primary estimand is the adjusted association between a donor-level
exposure and relative expression *within a cell type*. The workflow:

1.  takes raw counts and the donor of each cell from a container that
    has checked the donors against the exposure table;
2.  aggregates the sparse matrix by donor and cell type;
3.  retains the complete target-cell-type transcriptome library size;
4.  fixes expression support without inspecting exposure labels;
5.  applies TMM normalisation and robust edgeR quasi-likelihood
    inference;
6.  checks group support, design rank and numerical estimability; and
7.  adjusts across the full feature-by-cell-type hypothesis family.

The functions sum the counts as they are given and do not check that
they are raw: counts that were normalised or corrected beforehand are
summed like any others, and the models are then not the ones described
here.

Cell-type composition is a separate relative-composition outcome. It is
not an offset for the primary expression estimand, and captured cell
proportions are not absolute tissue abundance.

## Functions

| Group | Functions |
|----|----|
| Container | [`build_scee()`](reference/build_scee.md), [`as_scee()`](reference/as_scee.md) (from a rexposome `ExposomeSet`), [`seurat_to_exposure()`](reference/seurat_to_exposure.md), [`exposure_impute_lod()`](reference/exposure_impute_lod.md); accessors [`exposureData()`](reference/SCEE-accessors.md), [`exposureInfo()`](reference/SCEE-accessors.md), [`exposureVariables()`](reference/SCEE-accessors.md), [`sampleColumn()`](reference/SCEE-accessors.md), [`cellSampleMap()`](reference/SCEE-accessors.md) |
| Primary analysis | [`run_sc_exwas()`](reference/run_sc_exwas.md) (edgeR, DESeq2 or voom-dream backends), [`donor_pseudobulk()`](reference/donor_pseudobulk.md), [`run_sc_exwas_pb_offset()`](reference/run_sc_exwas_pb_offset.md), [`run_multi_exwas()`](reference/run_multi_exwas.md), [`run_sc_exwas_glmm()`](reference/run_sc_exwas_glmm.md), [`run_meta_exwas()`](reference/run_meta_exwas.md) |
| Design | [`estimate_power()`](reference/estimate_power.md) |
| Exposure modelling | [`run_dose_response()`](reference/run_dose_response.md), [`run_dose_response_gam()`](reference/run_dose_response_gam.md), [`run_interaction_test()`](reference/run_interaction_test.md), [`run_mixture_qgcomp()`](reference/run_mixture_qgcomp.md), [`run_sc_mixture()`](reference/run_sc_mixture.md) |
| Composition | [`run_exposure_composition()`](reference/run_exposure_composition.md) |
| Downstream | [`run_gsea()`](reference/run_gsea.md), [`run_cell_coupling()`](reference/run_cell_coupling.md) |
| Cross-omic networks (exploratory) | [`simulate_crossomic_network()`](reference/simulate_crossomic_network.md), [`run_celltype_network()`](reference/run_celltype_network.md), [`run_exposure_network()`](reference/run_exposure_network.md), [`run_comparative_network()`](reference/run_comparative_network.md) and their plots |

The network functions fit sparse Gaussian graphical models with the
graphical lasso and the collaborative graphical lasso. An edge is a
summary under that model for the donors analysed, not a tested
conditional independence, and
[`run_comparative_network()`](reference/run_comparative_network.md)
describes the differences between networks without testing them. The
package estimates associations; it does not supply causal
identification.

## HLCA data provenance

The airway data come from the integrated HLCA collection of Sikkema *et
al.* (2023), distributed under CC BY 4.0 through CZ CELLxGENE.

| Item | Pinned source |
|----|----|
| Publication | [Sikkema *et al.*, *Nature Medicine* (2023)](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41591-023-02327-2) |
| CELLxGENE collection | [Integrated Human Lung Cell Atlas](https://cellxgene.cziscience.com/collections/6f6d381a-7701-4781-935c-db10d30de293) |
| Exact H5AD asset | [688185ad-11c2-4172-a53a-f4f1f4076860.h5ad](https://datasets.cellxgene.cziscience.com/688185ad-11c2-4172-a53a-f4f1f4076860.h5ad) |
| Count layer | `/raw/X`; `/X` is not used for count modelling |
| H5AD SHA-256 | `1cbdde1e513a31bdb6a3f70296e2d0612760d2af4032e239c94596ea87b44007` |

The example data set shipped with the package,
`inst/extdata/hlca_airway_subset.rds`, is taken from this file: 352
cells of 12 donors of its study `Seibold_2020`, which is [Goldfarbmuren
*et al.*, *Nature Communications*
(2020)](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-020-16239-z).
`inst/scripts/make_hlca_airway_subset.R` checks the size and the SHA-256
of the H5AD and makes the subset from it; cells and genes are selected
and the counts are unchanged. The subset is redistributed under the same
CC BY 4.0 licence.

The scripts that prepare the full ever- versus never-smoking analysis
object are installed with the package, in the directory that
`system.file("scripts", package = "exposomeSC")` returns. `fetch_hlca.R`
rejects a missing raw layer, a changed asset size, and non-finite,
negative or non-integer values. Each script takes the paths of its
inputs and of its output as arguments; `create_hlca_input_manifest.R`
takes first the directory, here `.`, in which it writes
`hlca_input_manifest.rds` and `hlca_input_manifest.csv`. With the pinned
H5AD downloaded as `hlca_core.h5ad`:

``` sh
scripts=$(Rscript -e 'cat(system.file("scripts", package = "exposomeSC"))')
Rscript "$scripts/fetch_hlca.R" hlca_core.h5ad hlca_smoking_scee.rds
Rscript "$scripts/extract_hlca_design_metadata.R" hlca_core.h5ad \
    hlca_design_metadata.rds
Rscript "$scripts/extract_hlca_feature_metadata.R" hlca_core.h5ad \
    hlca_feature_metadata.rds
Rscript "$scripts/create_hlca_input_manifest.R" . hlca_core.h5ad \
    hlca_smoking_scee.rds hlca_design_metadata.rds hlca_feature_metadata.rds
```

The scripts need rhdf5, zellkonverter, AnnotationDbi, org.Hs.eg.db and
digest, which the package itself does not depend on.

## INCOV data provenance

The second data set, `inst/extdata/incov_pbmc_subset.rds`, is taken from
the INCOV cohort of [Su *et al.*, *Cell*
(2020)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2020.10.037): 1,032 blood
mononuclear cells of 43 patients with COVID-19 at their first blood
draw, with the counts of 192 antibodies for the same cells (four of them
isotype controls), 182 plasma metabolites and the plasma levels of 13
compounds of exogenous origin.

| Item | Source |
|----|----|
| Clinical records, plasma metabolites | Table S1 of [Mendeley Data, doi:10.17632/tzydswhhb5.5](https://doi.org/10.17632/tzydswhhb5.5), version 5, CC BY 4.0 |
| Single-cell genes and surface proteins | [ArrayExpress E-MTAB-9357](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/biostudies/arrayexpress/studies/E-MTAB-9357), redistributed under CC BY 4.0 with the permission of the authors who deposited it |

`inst/scripts/make_incov_pbmc_subset.R` checks the size and the SHA-256
of the 88 input files, recovers the counts from the logarithms that the
archive holds, assigns monocytes and T cells by gates on surface
proteins and marker genes, and draws the cells;
[`?incov_pbmc_subset`](reference/incov_pbmc_subset.md) describes each
step. It takes the folder with the input files and the output file as
arguments and needs data.table and R.utils.

## Documentation

- [exposomeSC](vignettes/exposomeSC.Rmd): the container, the association
  model and the further analyses, each run on one of the two real data
  sets of the package
- [Network tutorial](vignettes/network-tutorial.Rmd): exploratory
  cross-omic networks of two cell types and plasma metabolites, and
  their descriptive comparison, run on the INCOV data
- [Permutation and power](vignettes/permutation-and-power.Rmd): checks
  of a result on the airway data, by permuting the exposure among the
  donors and by a second backend, the two adjustments of the p-values,
  and a power approximation

On every push to `main`, GitHub Actions run `R CMD check` on Linux,
macOS and Windows, `BiocCheck`, the test coverage and a check of the
citation, the links and the spelling; the workflows are in
`.github/workflows`.

## Licence and citation

The code and the documentation of the package are under Artistic-2.0.
The two data files in `inst/extdata` are not: they are parts of the data
of others and are redistributed under CC BY 4.0.
`hlca_airway_subset.rds` keeps the licence of the atlas. In
`incov_pbmc_subset.rds` the clinical records and plasma measurements are
under CC BY 4.0 as published on Mendeley Data, and for the single-cell
counts, from ArrayExpress E-MTAB-9357, the authors who deposited them
gave this permission on 21 November 2026:

> The single-cell values from E-MTAB-9357 included in exposomeSC may be
> used and redistributed under CC BY 4.0, with citation of Su et
> al. (2020).

The two provenance sections above and the help pages of the data sets
name the sources and the publications to cite.

To cite the package, use `citation("exposomeSC")`: it gives the
Bioconductor DOI,
[10.18129/B9.bioc.exposomeSC](https://doi.org/10.18129/B9.bioc.exposomeSC),
and the version installed. When you use the shipped data sets, please
cite their primary publications as well.

## Example data

- [`hlca_airway_subset`](hlca_airway_subset.md) : Airway epithelial
  cells of smokers and never smokers from the Human Lung Cell Atlas
- [`incov_pbmc_subset`](incov_pbmc_subset.md) : Blood cells, surface
  proteins and plasma measurements of patients with COVID-19 from the
  INCOV cohort

## Association of an exposure with expression

Donor-pseudobulk models within cell types, and the models and analyses
built on them

- [`run_sc_exwas()`](run_sc_exwas.md) : Run cell-type-specific ExWAS
- [`run_multi_exwas()`](run_multi_exwas.md) : Run sc-ExWAS across
  multiple exposures
- [`run_interaction_test()`](run_interaction_test.md) : Test
  exposure-by-celltype interaction
- [`run_sc_exwas_pb_offset()`](run_sc_exwas_pb_offset.md) : Donor
  offset-pseudobulk negative-binomial sc-ExWAS
- [`run_sc_exwas_glmm()`](run_sc_exwas_glmm.md) : Cell-level linear
  mixed model sc-ExWAS with finite-df inference
- [`run_meta_exwas()`](run_meta_exwas.md) : Meta-analysis across cohorts
  for sc-ExWAS
- [`run_gsea()`](run_gsea.md) : Gene set enrichment on sc-ExWAS results

## Dose and response

- [`run_dose_response()`](run_dose_response.md) : Cell-type-specific
  exposure dose-response analysis
- [`run_dose_response_gam()`](run_dose_response_gam.md) : GAM-based
  dose-response analysis

## Mixtures of exposures

- [`run_sc_mixture()`](run_sc_mixture.md) : Cell-type-specific mixture
  exposure analysis
- [`run_mixture_qgcomp()`](run_mixture_qgcomp.md) : Formal mixture
  analysis via quantile g-computation

## Cell composition and gene-protein coupling

- [`run_exposure_composition()`](run_exposure_composition.md) : Test
  exposure associations with donor-level cell composition
- [`run_cell_coupling()`](run_cell_coupling.md) : Cell-Level
  Gene-Protein Coupling Analysis

## Exposure measurements and study planning

- [`exposure_impute_lod()`](exposure_impute_lod.md) : Impute exposure
  values below the limit of detection
- [`estimate_power()`](estimate_power.md) : Power analysis for sc-ExWAS
  study design
